papers.title: Amyloid/RNA Condensates with Germ Granule Characteristics Are Present in Rat Epididymal Spermatozoa and Exhibit Prion-Like Propagation Activity
papers.abstract: Environmental exposures to the germline can alter its epigenome resulting in new traits being acquired by offspring. While the epigenetic carrier in mammalian spermatozoa remains unknown, studies in C.elegans show that amyloids and sperm-specific populations of germ granules, phase-separated biomolecular condensates enriched in RNA-binding proteins and small noncoding RNAs, transmit heritable epigenetic phenotypes to descendant cells. Here we discovered that rat epididymal spermatozoa contain germ granule-like condensates in the head perforatorium, a cytoplasmic derived structure that participates in early post-fertilization events. The perforatoria condensates contain evolutionarily conserved germ granule markers and small noncoding RNAs and are enriched in amyloid, including those of the clinically relevant amyloidogenic proteins androgen receptor (AR) and TDP43. Further, perforatoria extracts exhibit prion-like propagation behavior by functioning as molecular seeds to template amyloid assembly in recombinant AR and TDP43. We propose that nature has conserved sperm germ granule-like structures throughout evolution to allow an organism to respond and adapt to a changed environment by passing environmentally encoded information to the embryo via a non-Mendelian protein-based mechanism of inheritance.

papers.title: An Ovol1 Variant in Endothelial Cells Regulates Slug and is Essential for Pathological Angiogenesis
papers.abstract: During development, the blood vasculature expands by sprouting angiogenesis, but the programs that guide this process can become dysregulated in the pathological angiogenesis of neovascular diseases leading to excessive disorganized blood vessels. We previously reported that in endothelial cells, the pro-mesenchymal transcription factor Slug critically regulates angiogenesis through a partial and reversible endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (pEndoMT); however, the upstream regulators that activate Slug and may contribute to pathological activation of the pEndoMT pathway in disease are still poorly understood. Here, we show that endothelial cells express an unusual low molecular weight variant of Ovol1 - a zinc-finger transcription factor that regulates mesenchymal transition in epithelial cells. Ovol1 and Slug are co-expressed in angiogenic endothelial cells, and using ChIP, we confirm direct Ovol1 binding to the endogenous Slug gene at a species-conserved binding motif. Whereas Ovol1 is typically a transcriptional repressor in epithelial cells, we find using a combination of silencing RNA and lentiviral overexpression constructs that the endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug, and is sufficient to drive pEndoMT marker expression and enhance endothelial cell migratory capacity. Silencing of Ovol1 abolished sprouting angiogenesis in a 3D in vitro sprouting angiogenesis assay, whereas constitutive overexpression of Ovol1 produced overaggressive and disorganized hypersprouting that depends upon Slug. We generated Ovol1 or Slug endothelial-specific knockout mice (Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO) and found that healthy developmental angiogenesis of the neonatal mouse retina proceeds relatively normally in knockout animals. By contrast, Ovol1 was reduced in established post-natal blood vessels but became strongly re-expressed in tumor endothelial cells, and we found that colorectal cancer syngraft growth was significantly reduced in both Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO mice alongside a failure of tumor angiogenesis. Lastly, neovascularization in the oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) model was also reduced in SlugECKO mice. In conclusion, we report that an endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug and drives a mesenchymal-like state, and that this Ovol1-Slug pEndoMT signaling axis is essential for pathological angiogenesis in neovascular disease models.

papers.title: CardioShift: Resolving cell-to-cell functional heterogeneity in hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from high-throughput single-cell imaging
papers.abstract: High-content screening of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) is widely used for disease modeling, yet standard pipelines rely on whole-well averages that obscure cell-to-cell heterogeneity. Moving from well-averages to single-cell analysis reveals hidden variations, but may introduce a pseudoreplication bias if cells are analysed as independent data points. We present CardioShift, an open-source bioimage informatics framework designed to map single-cell distributions by properly accounting for this nested variance structure. Applying this framework to 32,818 Ca2+ transients and 10,719 contractility-lipid profiles, we show that cell-to-cell variability represents the largest source of variance for most functional parameters, demonstrating how traditional well averages mask condition-dependent phenotypes. Furthermore, unsupervised clustering identifies condition-dependent shifts in functional subpopulations, including a distinct cellular state that accumulates lipids but maintains baseline contraction kinetics that was not detected using well- and single-cell averaging approaches. CardioShift provides a robust analytical approach to resolve hidden single-cell distributions.

papers.title: KH1 Domain of Poly C Binding Protein 1 (PCBP1) Interacts with Utrophin-A mRNA and Modulates Utrophin-A Expression in Mouse Myoblasts
papers.abstract: Utrophin upregulation is an attractive strategy to ameliorate Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). Here, we investigated whether the murine poly(C)-binding protein 1 (PCBP1) directly interacts with the utrophin-A mRNA, and how the interaction shapes the fate of utrophin-A in muscle cells. As no experimentally validated structure of the murine PCBP1 is available, AlphaFold2 was utilized to predict the structure of the full-length protein and the KH1-KH2 domain of the protein. The more stable and reliable model of the KH1-KH2 domain of PCBP1 was then docked with the 5'UTR of the utrophin-A mRNA, and the top-ranked docked complex was utilized for MD simulation to identify the most stable hydrogen bond-forming amino acid residues from PCBP1. ITC showed a thermodynamically favorable spontaneous interaction between the full-length PCBP1 and the 5'UTR of utrophin-A mRNA, but the deletion mutant of PCBP1, lacking the predicted contact region, failed to exhibit any interaction. This observation was also confirmed by an RNA-immunoprecipitation assay in C2C12 cells. However, the mutant PCBP1 was unable to alter the expression of the utrophin-A in the C2C12 cells. In cells, PCBP1 overexpression lowered utrophin-A expression, while shRNA knockdown produced reciprocal increases. A 5'UTR-luciferase reporter mirrored this observation. Finally, subcellular fractionation showed that PCBP1 promotes nuclear retention of utrophin-A transcripts and reduces their cytoplasmic availability, with reciprocal shifts upon PCBP1 knockdown. Considering earlier work on PCBP2, our data suggest both paralogs recognize the same 5'UTR element, and the KH1-dependent interaction represses utrophin-A by coupling nuclear retention to reduced protein output. Thus, the PCBP1-5'UTR interaction emerges as a potent target for utrophin de-repression in DMD.

papers.title: HER3 mediates metabolic reprogramming in metastatic colorectal and pancreatic cancer
papers.abstract: Liver metastases are a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet the oncogenic signals that shape tumor metabolism in the hepatic niche remain poorly understood. Here, we show that HER3 activation drives a liver metastasis-specific glycolytic program in both cancer types. Genetic or pharmacological HER3 inhibition suppresses cancer glycolysis while increasing dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), rendering liver metastases vulnerable to OXPHOS inhibition. Combining the HER3 inhibitor sapitinib with distinct OXPHOS inhibitors led to in vitro synergy and durable tumor-free survival in orthotopic CRC and PDAC liver metastases models, with further validation in patient-derived xenografts. Mechanistically, HER3 promotes glycolysis through activating PFK2 and reduces OXPHOS through activating DRP1-mediated mitochondrial remodeling, both pathways were activated in liver metastases compared to matched primary tumors. Together, our findings identify the HER3-AKT/RSK-PFK2 axis as a driver of glycolysis and metastatic growth and reveal an OXPHOS dependency induced by HER3 inhibition that may be exploited through combined HER3 and OXPHOS targeting in metastatic CRC and PDAC.

papers.title: Seesaw configuration of the ODC-OAZ1-AZIN1 axis governs sensitivity to polyamine-targeting inhibitors of breast cancer cells
papers.abstract: Polyamines are endogenous metabolites crucial for various cellular functions, and maintaining their cellular levels is critical for normal cell survival and fate. Polyamine homeostasis is managed by a complex metabolic network, wherein the ODC-OAZ1-AZIN1 protein-protein interaction axis plays a central role in regulating polyamine synthesis and membrane transport. While existing research has established that polyamine-targeted inhibitors (PTIs) significantly perturb this axis in various cancers, and that different breast cancer subtypes display distinct PTI sensitivities, the fundamental mechanism of drug sensitivity difference has remained poorly understood. Here, we combine large-scale bioinformatic analysis with comprehensive experimental verification to reveal a polarized seesaw configuration of the ODC-OAZ1-AZIN1 axis across diverse tumor types, including breast cancer. We show that this seesaw configuration is not only distinct across breast cancer subtypes but also associated with unique cellular states. Furthermore, we reveal that this configuration underpins the distinct sensitivity profiles of these subtypes to both single and combination treatments of PTIs. Crucially, we demonstrate that targeted re-configuration of this axis can shift the drug sensitivity of resistant cells. This study provides the first systematic mechanistic framework linking the configuration of the ODC-OAZ1-AZIN1 axis to PTI sensitivity, thereby providing a configuration-based framework for rational selection of PTI combination regimens and new personalized therapeutic strategies in breast cancer.

papers.title: Serotonin signals through ciliary 5-HT6 to control insulin secretion
papers.abstract: In the pancreatic islet, serotonin (5-HT) functions basally to modulate glucagon secretion, but its contribution to beta-cell signaling and function remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that the Gs-coupled serotonin receptor 6 (5-HT6), previously thought to be expressed almost exclusively in the brain, localizes to the primary cilium and plasma membrane of islet cells and augments insulin secretion. Utilizing a transgenic model of beta-cell cilia loss, along with approaches to perturb cilia-specific 5-HT6 function without disrupting the native cilium architecture, we show that 5-HT6 action in beta cells is dependent on the primary cilium. Critically, the plasma membrane pool of 5-HT6 cannot stimulate insulin release when the cilium is absent, representing an instance of whole-cell regulation by a cilia-localized GPCR. These findings establish subcellular localization as a determinant of GPCR function in beta cells and identify ciliary 5-HT6 signaling as a distinct pathway for modulating insulin secretion.

papers.title: A cotranslational role for selenocysteine in productive protein folding
papers.abstract: Selenocysteine (Sec) is generally regarded as the catalytic determinant that distinguishes selenoproteins from their cysteine (Cys)-containing counterparts. Consequently, the biological significance of Sec has largely been attributed to its unique chemical properties within mature proteins. Here, we uncover an unexpected role for Sec in protein biogenesis. Using the endoplasmic reticulum selenoprotein SELENOM as a model, we show that replacement of Sec with Cys redirects the protein into an alternative assembly pathway, resulting in formation of a stable domain-swapped homodimer. Biochemical and structural analyses demonstrate that this phenotype cannot be explained solely by altered active-site chemistry, as dimerisation persists following extensive active-site mutagenesis. Remarkably, reintroduction of Sec at alternative positions suppresses dimer formation, including when Sec is placed within a cleaved signal peptide and is absent from the mature protein. Thus, identical protein sequences can adopt distinct folding outcomes depending on whether Sec incorporation occurred during biosynthesis. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised role for Sec in productive protein folding and raise the possibility that evolutionary retention of the Sec incorporation pathway reflects advantages not only in catalysis but also in protein folding.

papers.title: Cell-lineage selection interacts with development and life history to shape the rates and identity of heritable mutations
papers.abstract: Mutation rates determine the supply of heritable variation and are central to evolutionary theory, yet they are usually treated as properties of molecular mutational processes. We hypothesised that mutation rates are also shaped by selection among cell lineages within organisms and that the strength of this process depends on developmental and life-history traits. To test the extent of this idea, we combined mathematical modelling with experiments in Drosophila melanogaster and treated mutation rates as emergent properties of interactions among molecular mutagenesis, development, life history, and cell-lineage selection. The model predicts that even modest effects of mutations on cellular fitness can substantially alter the probability that mutations are transmitted, and that these effects depend strongly on developmental architecture, germline dynamics, and time to reproduction. In Drosophila, we experimentally demonstrate biased transmission of a mutation affecting cellular proliferation and show that this bias changes over the reproductive lifespan of the individual. Extending the model genome-wide reveals that the cellular distribution of fitness effects and its interaction with developmental parameters influence both the estimated mutation rate and the composition of transmitted mutations, producing transmission biases that favour mutations with particular cellular fitness effects. These results suggest that developmental and life-history parameters determine how cellular fitness effects translate into transmission bias; therefore, estimates of heritable mutational input can vary from species to species even under constant molecular mutagenesis. By filtering mutations before they enter populations, developmental and life-history evolution can modify both the rate and the nature of heritable variation and thereby influence evolutionary trajectories.

papers.title: The pupal stage shapes life-history trade-offs across metamorphosis
papers.abstract: Dealing with ecological stressors during development often comes at the expense of later-life performance. Although such trade-offs are well studied as two-stage systems such as larva-adult trade-offs, they are rarely examined across multiple developmental stages, limiting our understanding of how ecological effects are integrated throughout complex life cycles. We addressed this gap using a multistage experimental framework in Aedes aegypti, where we exposed individuals to predation risk during the larval stage, the pupal stage, both stages, or neither, and quantified developmental, physiological, and adult fitness traits. Contrary to expectations, predation risk across successive stages did not produce cumulative fitness costs, and traits varied in their responses. Both males and females emerged faster when exposed to risk, with lighter bodies, but males paid an additional cost of reduced starvation resistance when the pupal stage was exposed. Surprisingly, despite their lower body mass, females showed enhanced reproductive performance when both stages were exposed to risk. Overall, responses were stage- and sex-specific, with exposure during the non-feeding pupal stage imposing greater life-history costs than larval exposure alone. Measurements across the larva-pupa-adult continuum further revealed that traits such as body mass and energy reserves respond differently before and after metamorphosis, highlighting the role of the pupa in mediating trade-offs. Our findings identify the pupal stage as a critical mediator of life-history trade-offs and demonstrate the value of a multistage framework for understanding the role of each stage in life-history evolution.

papers.title: Adipocyte Kindlin-2 Coordinates an E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2 Endocrine Axis to Regulate Skin Regeneration and Diabetic Wound Healing
papers.abstract: Skin wound healing is a complex, multicellular process essential for maintaining tissue integrity and homeostasis. Despite advances in biomaterial and cell-based therapies, the mechanisms by which adipose tissue regulates skin regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify adipocyte Kindlin-2 as a critical regulator of cutaneous wound repair. Adipocyte-specific deletion of Kindlin-2 markedly accelerates wound closure in mice by enhancing fibroblast proliferation, angiogenesis, and suppressing inflammation. Transplantation of visceral white adipose tissue (vWAT) from Kindlin-2-deficient mice similarly promotes wound healing, indicating an endocrine contribution of vWAT to skin regeneration. Mechanistically, loss of Kindlin-2 promotes E-cadherin proteolysis, resulting in increased release of a 33-kDa C-terminal fragment (CTF2) that activates {beta}-catenin signaling and induces transcriptional upregulation and secretion of insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2). Elevated circulating IGFBP2, in turn, stimulates integrin signaling in target cells to enhance wound repair. Pharmacological inhibition of {beta}-catenin signaling abrogated the healing advantage conferred by Kindlin-2 deficiency. Conversely, local delivery of IGFBP2 via lentiviral significantly accelerates wound closure in both wild-type C57BL/6 and diabetic ob/ob mice. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized adipose-skin endocrine axis governed by Kindlin-2 and IGFBP2 that orchestrates tissue regeneration. Targeting this Kindlin-2/E-cadherin/{beta}-catenin/IGFBP2 pathway offers a promising therapeutic strategy for enhancing wound healing, particularly in chronic and diabetic wounds.

papers.title: SDHB deficiency silences ABCB1 expression and confers therapeutic vulnerability across multiple cancer types
papers.abstract: Succinate dehydrogenase B (SDHB)-deficient cancers, including pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL), renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), exhibit aggressive clinical behavior with limited treatment options. To identify novel therapeutic vulnerabilities, we performed high-throughput drug screening using co-cultured human SDHB-deficient and SDHB-reconstituted UOK269 human renal cell carcinoma cells with dual fluorescence labeling. Several compounds displaying preferential cytotoxicity toward SDHB-deficient cells were known substrates of the ATP-binding cassette B1 (ABCB1) transporter, also known as Multidrug Resistance Protein 1 (MDR1). Accordingly, SDHB-deficient cells demonstrated markedly reduced ABCB1 expression, a phenotype confirmed across human SDHB-deficient PPGL, RCC, and GIST samples, but absent in IDH- or FH-deficient tumors. Mechanistic investigation revealed that KDM4A histone demethylase is downregulated in SDHB-deficient tumors, and KDM4A loss (or inhibition) is sufficient to reduce ABCB1 expression, globally increase H3K9me3 levels, and sensitize cells to cytotoxic ABCB1 substrates. TCGA analysis confirmed correlated KDM4A-ABCB1 expression in SDHB-deficient cancers, with ABCB1 levels predicting drug sensitivity across cancer cell lines. Clinical analysis demonstrated that SDHB-mutant PPGL patients treated with vincristine-containing chemotherapy exhibited significantly longer progression-free survival compared to non-SDHB patients. These findings establish a novel metabolic-epigenetic pathway linking SDHB deficiency to ABCB1 silencing and provide rational basis for repurposing vincristine, and related ABCB1 substrate vinca alkaloids, across SDHB-deficient cancer types; offering an alternative precision treatment approach for these challenging malignancies.

papers.title: A mouse model of metastasis-induced breast cancer cachexia with non-cachectic controls bearing isogenic primary tumors
papers.abstract: Background Patients with advanced cancer frequently develop cachexia, an involuntary weight-loss condition that correlates strongly with metastatic burden. Despite this clinical association, metastasis is rarely considered in preclinical research of cancer cachexia, which is in part due to the lack of rigorously established animal models to investigate metastasis-associated cancer cachexia. Methods To establish an animal model of metastasis-associated cancer cachexia, here we focused on syngeneic mouse models of breast cancer. Using the metastatic 4T1 murine breast cancer cell line and its isogenic non-metastatic 67NR cell line, we generated primary tumors via orthotopic injection into the mammary fat pad and surgically resected the primary tumor to allow sufficient time for spontaneous metastatic outgrowth, or generated experimental lung metastases by direct intravenous injection into the tail vein. Across these tumor-bearing groups, we systematically characterized the metastatic burden and cachectic phenotypes of the mice, including body weight, food intake, body composition, muscle mass, grip strength, locomotor activity, energy expenditure, and respiratory exchange ratio. To isolate the contribution of reduced food intake to the cachectic phenotypes, we pair-fed orthotopic 4T1 tumor-bearing mice (which were non-cachectic) to mice with 4T1 lung metastases (which were cachectic). We further measured muscle atrophy gene expression and profiled circulating cytokines and metabolic hormones for the mouse groups. Results Body weight loss occurred exclusively in mice bearing lung metastases from 4T1 tumors, with no weight loss observed in mice bearing either primary 4T1 tumors or 67NR lung tumors, thus presenting a model of cancer cachexia that is driven by 4T1 lung metastasis. Comprehensive cachexia characterization demonstrated that the 4T1 metastasis model recapitulates all key features of cachexia, manifesting as reduced food intake (or anorexia), depletion of adipose tissues, loss of lean mass including muscle mass loss, and reduced grip strength. Pair-feeding non-cachectic primary 4T1 tumor-bearing mice to 4T1 metastatic mice led to the same losses in body weight, fat, and lean mass as in cachectic mice, but no change in grip strength, indicating that anorexia is the primary driver of tissue wasting whereas muscle weakness arises through a food intake-independent mechanism. Moreover, we identified distinct circulating cytokines and metabolic hormones associated with the metastasis-driven cachexia. Conclusions Our results establish a metastasis-induced breast cancer cachexia model with a tightly matched control group, providing a platform for the field to identify metastasis-derived cachectic mediators and pathways.

papers.title: PERTURBATION OF THE AMINO ACID STRESS RESPONSE PATHWAY EXPOSES A METABOLIC VULNERABILITY IN MULTIPLE AGGRESSIVE CANCER SUBTYPES
papers.abstract: Cancer cells frequently experience nutrient limitation and depend on adaptive stress-response pathways to maintain metabolic homeostasis. Here, we show that pharmacological perturbation of amino acid stress signaling exerts broad anti-tumor activity across multiple aggressive malignancies, including acute lymphoblastic leukemia, acute myeloid leukemia, triple-negative breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and neuroblastoma. Sensitivity to pathway modulation is associated with a chronic stress-adapted metabolic state marked by constitutive amino acid response signaling, elevated NFE2L2 expression, and reduced mitochondrial abundance despite evidence of efficient oxidative metabolism. Mechanistically, we demonstrate that the ATP-competitive compound GCN2-IN-6 does not phenocopy genetic GCN2 suppression and exhibits context-dependent effects on the amino acid stress response. Nevertheless, tumors experiencing chronic metabolic stress remain exquisitely sensitive to disruption of this adaptive network, regardless of whether signaling is perturbed through canonical inhibition or paradoxical activation. Collectively, our findings identify chronic metabolic stress adaptation as an actionable vulnerability and establish off-balancing amino acid stress signaling as a therapeutic strategy across multiple cancer types

papers.title: Bispecific VSV-G Engagers: A Platform for Cell-Type-Specific Delivery of Viral Vectors
papers.abstract: VSV-G-pseudotyped lentiviral vectors (LVVs) enable highly efficient ex vivo gene delivery through the broadly expressed LDL receptor (LDLR) but lack the cell-type specificity required for in vivo applications. To provide cell-type specificity, we developed reversible engagers consisting of a cell-specific ligand or antibody fused to the ~40-amino-acid VSV-G-binding domains of LDLR. Following endocytosis, the engager dissociates, releasing unmodified VSV-G for efficient delivery of the vector cargo. An engager comprising the CEACAM8 N-terminal domain enables selective transduction of CEACAM6-positive epithelial cells. A trimeric CEACAM8-based engager matching the VSV-G homotrimeric spike blocked non-specific VSV infection through LDLR with an IC50 of 16.7 pM, while enabling effective VSV-mediated lysis of CEACAM6-positive tumor cells. An anti-CD3-based trimeric engager selectively transduced non-preactivated T cells in human PBMCs with high transduction efficiency. Engager-mediated in vivo CAR T cell generation resulted in sustained control of human OPM2 multiple myeloma tumors in NSG mice. This platform may further advance in vivo gene therapy, including in vivo CAR T-cell therapy and tumor-directed oncolytic virotherapy.

papers.title: Comparative Oogenesis in Annual and Non-annual African Killifishes: Oocyte Staging in the Fastest-Aging Vertebrate, Nothobranchius furzeri
papers.abstract: Annual killifishes have evolved specialized reproductive strategies that allow their embryos to survive the seasonal desiccation of ephemeral habitats, yet little is known about how these adaptations arise during oogenesis. We hypothesized that traits contributing to embryonic desiccation resistance may originate from modifications in the follicular wall and egg envelope during oocyte development. Here, we provide a comparative morphological and morphometric characterization of oogenesis in the annual African turquoise killifish Nothobranchius furzeri and the non-annual lyretail killifish Aphyosemion australe, from early oocyte development through Primary Growth (PG), Secondary Growth (SG), Maturation, and Ovulation. Despite their contrasting life histories, both species exhibited a highly conserved sequence of oocyte development. Cortical alveoli accumulated before oil droplets during PG, whereas SG was characterized by the progressive coalescence of yolk globules into a homogeneous fluid yolk mass and the peripheral displacement of oil droplets and cortical alveoli. Oocyte diameter did not differ significantly between species at any developmental stage, and the follicular epithelium followed a similar developmental pattern, suggesting that its basic morphological organization is conserved despite contrasting reproductive ecologies. In contrast, greater interspecific divergence was observed in the zona pellucida, which became significantly thicker in N. furzeri from early SG through Maturation and exhibited distinct patterns of chorionic ornamentation between species. These findings reveal a largely conserved program of oogenesis and follicular epithelial differentiation in annual and non-annual African killifishes, while highlighting greater morphological divergence in the egg envelope. This suggests that different components of the ovarian follicle may exhibit distinct degrees of evolutionary plasticity, with modifications of the zona pellucida potentially contributing to embryo-environment interactions and desiccation resistance in annual species.

papers.title: Stochastic and Heritable Responses in Cell-Size Regulation and Survival to pH Stress in C. glutamicum
papers.abstract: Bacterial survival in fluctuating environments depends on the ability of individual cells to maintain physiological homeostasis under stress, yet how single cells recover from transient pH fluctuations remains poorly understood. We tracked the cell-size dynamics and survival of Corynebacterium glutamicum cells exposed to short, strong acid (pH 4, 20 min) or alkaline (pH 11, 15 min) pulses. Acid stress considerably increases the size added during the stress cycle, whereas alkaline stress increases it only modestly. Nevertheless, surviving cells maintain their division strategy and restore size homeostasis in the next cycle. Coordination between relatives is short-lived: sister cells have similar cell-cycle durations after stress, but durations become uncorrelated once the last division shared by two cells precedes the stress by more than about 1.5 generations. Survival of acid stress favors larger cells and is largely stochastic, with no detectable lineage heritability. In contrast, survival of alkaline stress favors smaller cells and is transiently heritable: co-survival probability remains high among relatives separated by up to two generations. These findings provide insight into pH survival in C. glutamicum and present statistical methods to study cell-size regulation and survival under transient, severe environmental fluctuations.

papers.title: A Systems Theory of Cardiac-Autonomic Trajectories and Equilibria
papers.abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) is conventionally summarized with static indices computed over fixed windows, which cannot show how cardiac autonomic regulation persists, transitions, responds to perturbation, and recovers. We develop the Systems Theory of Cardiac-Autonomic Trajectories and Equilibria (STATE), in which autonomic regulation is a low-dimensional latent stochastic dynamical system observed only through RR intervals, and we derive what the theory can and cannot claim. First, we prove that for isotropic linear dynamics the sympathetic and parasympathetic coordinates are not separately identifiable from a scalar RR signal, whereas distinct time scales or coupling restore observability. Second, we derive exact properties of a minimal bistable system (stationary law, mean escape time, critical forcing), and a Monte Carlo simulation agreed with the exact escape time within 6%. Third, in 2000 simulated replicates of a monostable and a bistable system that share the same linearization at rest, baseline variability (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, AUC, 0.56) and peak displacement at the pulse used (AUC 0.42) did not discriminate the systems, yet sustained return after an identical pulse differed: 100% versus 7%. We define resilience as a multidimensional response profile, show that recovery descriptors depend on analyst-chosen tolerances that must be fixed a priori, and state four falsifiable hypotheses with the result that would refute each. The work is theoretical and computational; no empirical recordings were used.

papers.title: Peripheral Axons Form Endoplasmic Reticulum-Rich Conduits With Breast Cancer Cells
papers.abstract: Peripheral nerves are active components of the tumor microenvironment, but the physical routes by which sensory axons communicate with cancer cells remain incompletely defined. Here, we show that primary dorsal root ganglion neurons form thin membrane conduits with EMT6 breast cancer cells that contain endoplasmic reticulum (ER). ER-Tracker labeling and neuron-restricted expression of the ER proteins CNPY2 and ATL3 identified ER-rich axonal extensions terminating on cancer cells. Serial-section scanning transmission electron microscopy resolved ER-like membranes within these conduits and at axon-cancer cell interfaces. Scanning electron microscopy and live holotomographic imaging further revealed dynamic contact formation and associated remodeling of the cancer cell surface. These observations define an ER-containing structural interface between sensory axons and cancer cells and provide a framework for testing whether neuronal ER contributes to direct intercellular signaling or material transfer.

papers.title: KobA mediates kinesin-1-dependent transport of dynein-dynactin to microtubule plus ends
papers.abstract: Cytoplasmic dynein transports diverse cargoes toward microtubule minus ends following activation by the dynactin complex and cargo adapters. In elongated cells such as fungal hyphae and neurons, dynein must first undergo kinesin-1-dependent transport to microtubule plus ends to engage cargoes, but the mechanism linking these opposing motors remains poorly understood. Here, we identify KobA in the filamentous fungus Aspergillus nidulans as a kinesin-1-binding, coiled-coil protein essential for kinesin-1 (KinA)-mediated plus-end transport of dynein and dynactin. KobA binds the C-terminal cargo-binding domain of KinA. Interestingly, KobA is not required for the general function of KinA in supporting hyphal growth alongside myosin-V, but is specifically required for the microtubule plus-end accumulation of dynein-dynactin even when KinA is activated. Mechanistically, KobA enhances the interaction between KinA and dynactin-dynein. Within its disordered N-terminal region, KobA harbors a Spindly motif typically present in dynein-activating cargo adapters that engage the dynactin pointed end. AlphaFold-3 predictions suggest that the Spindly motif of KobA also binds the dynactin pointed end, and in support of this notion, point mutations within the KobA Spindly motif disrupt the KinA-dynactin association, causing dynein to decorate microtubules rather than accumulate at plus ends. Together, our findings establish KobA as a novel adapter that utilizes a classic cargo adapter Spindly motif to link kinesin-1 to dynein-dynactin, ensuring targeted plus-end delivery of the minus-end motor.

papers.title: Long-range allosteric restraint by the Spiral-Pincer scaffold gates oxidative activation of the ATM kinase
papers.abstract: ATM is a master regulator of the DNA-damage response, activated either by DNA double-strand breaks through the MRN complex or, independently, by oxidative stress, which drives disulfide bond formation between Cys2991 residues on the two halves of the ATM dimer. Although both pathways involve release of the PIKK regulatory domain (PRD) from the kinase active site, how the distant Spiral--Pincer scaffold regulates access to this state remains unclear, partly because the PRD--FAT-TRD3 interface is unresolved in available experimental structures. Here, we combine an AlphaFold3-completed full-length ATM dimer model with well-tempered metadynamics to map its conformational landscape. We find that an oxidation-competent conformation already exists in the resting dimer, although it is rarely populated, supporting conformational selection rather than induction of a new state. Removing Spiral--Pincer eliminates this restriction: the conformation becomes dominant, and the landscape narrows to a few well-separated states. The dimer's two halves respond unequally, one loop of the PRD rearranging substantially while the other remains unchanged, via specific domain contacts rather than a direct route to the reactive cysteines. This identifies Spiral--Pincer as a release-controlled brake on ATM activation, a mechanism that may extend across the wider PIKK kinase family.

papers.title: Emergence and robustness of 3D complex tissue architectures from simple physical forces
papers.abstract: Although at central stake in biology and biological engineering, our understanding of how biological tissues acquire their architectures during morphogenesis and which mechanisms have been selected through evolution remain limited. Using adipose tissue as a biological model, we build a 3D mathematical model with simple mechanical rules between cells and fibers, and show that the model reproduces, in-silico, not only the emergence of complex and heterogeneous 3D architectures, but also the intra and inter-individual heterogeneities of shapes as observed in vivo. The model reveals that specific rules for cell differentiation are not necessary for tissue structuring, but could have been selected through evolution for robustness and efficiency. This study therefore suggests a paradigm shift where tissue architecture is an emerging process surprisingly more driven by mechanical processes than by complex predetermined molecular or genetic programs.

papers.title: CrJAMs are transcriptional repressors of the monoterpenoid indole alkaloid pathway in Catharanthus roseus
papers.abstract: Catharanthus roseus produces monoterpenoid indole alkaloids (MIAs) in response to the defense hormone jasmonate (JA). In Arabidopsis, JA regulates defense processes through MYC2 and JA-Associated MYC2a-like transcription factors (JAMs). Here we characterize two previously identified C. roseus JAMs, CrJAM2 and CrJAM3, as regulators of MIA biosynthesis. Functional screens using viral-induced gene silencing and transient promoter activity assays showed that CrJAMs repress the MIA pathway; silencing both CrJAM2 and CrJAM3 increased expression of MIA pathway genes and MIA levels while their individual overexpression repressed promoter activity. To assess their activity broadly across MIA regulatory and biosynthetic genes, we generated C. roseus hairy root cultures either constitutively overexpressing individual CrJAMs or CRISPR-Cas9 creating mutations in multiple CrJAMs, and profiled their expression by RNA-Seq. CrJAM2 overexpression decreased expression of most MIA biosynthetic genes relative to the GUS control, while double mutant lines showed increased basal expression of these genes relative to non-targeting controls. Notably, methyl JA treatment perturbs this equilibrium, reversing these trends at 24 hrs in both CrJAM overexpression and mutant lines relative to basal conditions. In summary, CrJAMs broadly repress MIA regulatory and biosynthetic gene expression and together with CrJAZ and CrMYC2a regulates MIA biosynthesis.

papers.title: NRT2.2 is essential for nitrate uptake and carbon-nitrogen balance in Nannochloropsis oceanica
papers.abstract: Nitrate is the dominant nitrogen source for marine microalgae, yet how it is taken up remains poorly understood in many ecologically and biotechnologically relevant species. Here we show that NITRATE TRANSPORTER 2.2 (NRT2.2) is the principal nitrate transporter of the oleaginous marine microalga Nannochloropsis oceanica. N. oceanica encodes only two NRT2 proteins and, unlike land plants and green algae, lacks a recognizable homolog of NITRATE ASSIMILATION-RELATED 2 (NAR2), the partner protein that green-lineage NRT2s require for activity and plasma membrane targeting. CRISPR knock-outs and confocal imaging showed that NRT2.2 is located at the plasma membrane and is required for nitrate uptake, whereas its paralog NRT2.1 cannot compensate for its loss. When nitrate was resupplied after nitrogen starvation, nrt2.2 mutants did not take up nitrate and did not resume growth, while they recovered normally with ammonium. Their photosystem II efficiency fell below that of fully nitrogen-starved wild-type cells, and chlorophyll content was reduced, while total protein remained stable. Fixed carbon was redirected into storage, with lipids and carbohydrates accumulating above the levels of all strains after 3 days of nitrogen starvation. Loss of NRT2.2 therefore mimics a prolonged nitrogen starvation, even though nitrate is available. Because nitrate was present but could not be used, recovery from starvation depends on the capacity to take up nitrate, not only on its availability. In the ocean, where nitrate is depleted for long periods and resupplied episodically, NRT2.2 is thus likely to set how quickly Nannochloropsis can use new nitrate inputs and resume growth.

papers.title: Coupled Modeling of Tumor Volume and ctDNA Dynamics in HPV-Associated Anal Squamous Cell Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Response to anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in advanced HPV-associated anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) varies and is assessed by infrequent imaging that lags behind tumor biology. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can be sampled frequently and reflects near-real-time tumor activity yet is rarely built into mechanistic models of treatment response. Using longitudinal tumor volume and HPV ctDNA from 26 patients treated with pembrolizumab, we found that baseline ctDNA scores tracked tumor burden but did not distinguish responders from non-responders, whereas ctDNA after one treatment cycle had a higher relative decrease in responders, six weeks before the next scan. We developed an ordinary differential equation model linking tumor volume to the ctDNA released by tumor cells. Sensitivity, identifiability, and model-selection analyses reduced it to two patient-specific parameters, proliferation and shedding rates, which reproduced individual volume and ctDNA trajectories, including a transient ctDNA spike at treatment onset. Proliferation was faster in non-responders. This framework supports model-based, ctDNA-guided monitoring of immunotherapy response.

papers.title: HOT1 functions as a homodimer to promote ALT-permissive chromatin
papers.abstract: Telomere homeostasis is a tightly regulated and dynamic process sustained by a network of proteins that organize telomeric chromatin and safeguard chromosome stability. In ALT-positive cells, telomere maintenance relies on recombination-based mechanisms and is modulated by local chromatin states and epigenetic regulation. Here, we show that the telomeric binding protein HOT1 (HMBOX1) requires dimerization - depending both on interaction with the dimerization-mediators DYNLL1/2 and its intrinsic HNFp1 domain - for its stable association with telomeres in vivo. Loss of HOT1 leads to an epigenetic switch from H3K9acK14ac to H3K9me3 at telomeres accompanied by attenuated ALT activity as illustrated by reduced ALT recombination by-products (C-circles) and a decrease in telomere dysfunction-induced foci (TIFs). We further show via binding assays and cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) analyses that HOT1 directly interacts with telomeric nucleosomes, providing a molecular basis for its involvement in telomeric chromatin organization. Collectively, these findings suggest that HOT1 functions as a homodimer to promote a telomeric chromatin state that is highly permissive for ALT recombination.

papers.title: Extensive membrane lipid remodeling at the host-parasite interface of Toxoplasma gondii
papers.abstract: Phosphoinositides regulate diverse membrane trafficking and signaling events in eukaryotic cells, yet their transbilayer distribution remains largely unexplored, particularly at host-parasite membrane interfaces. Here, we determined the membrane leaflet localization of phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PtdIns(4)P) and phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PtdIns(4,5)P2) in Toxoplasma gondii using quick-freezing freeze-fracture replica labeling combined with phosphoinositide-specific probes. Both phosphoinositides were predominantly localized to the cytoplasmic leaflet of the parasite plasma membrane, whereas only weak labeling was detected in the inner membrane complex. PtdIns(4)P, but not PtdIns(4,5)P2, was additionally detected on intracellular vesicles, while mature micronemes lacked detectable labeling for either phosphoinositide. Surprisingly, both phosphoinositides exhibited nearly symmetric distributions between the two leaflets of the parasitophorous vacuole membrane (PVM), in striking contrast to their asymmetric localization in the parasite plasma membrane. Together with our previous demonstration that phosphatidylserine and phosphatidylethanolamine also lose their transbilayer asymmetry in the PVM, these findings indicate that the PVM undergoes global membrane lipid remodeling that extends from major phospholipids to phosphoinositides. We propose that this extensive lipid reorganization represents a defining structural feature of the apicomplexan PVM and provides a new framework for understanding membrane identity at the host-parasite interface.

papers.title: Cargo levels control endosomal PI(3)P homeostasis through direct feedback between SNX17 and MTM1
papers.abstract: The sorting of internalised cell surface proteins through the endosomal network is crucial for cellular function. Phosphatidylinositol-3-phosphate (PI(3)P) is a critical lipid identity cue for organising endosomal sorting but there is limited understanding of how PI(3)P homeostasis is regulated. Here, we show that free PI(3)P is segregated into distinct endosomal subdomains and that depletion of the disease-relevant lipid phosphatase Myotubularin1 (MTM1) leads to its accumulation and mis-segregation, impairing cargo recycling. Complementary imaging and reconstitution approaches show that MTM1 recruitment and activity are controlled by binding to the endosomal cargo adaptor SNX17. This interaction is mediated by sorting motifs in the C-Terminal tail of MTM1 and is in competition with the same sorting motifs in cargo that bind to SNX17. This competitive binding mechanistically links cargo sorting to PI(3)P depletion and because SNX17 is itself a PI(3)P effector, establishes negative feedback regulating local PI(3)P levels. Importantly, we demonstrate that this feedback couples endosomal cargo levels to PI(3)P depletion. We propose that cargo levels thereby modulate endosomal phosphoinositide identity through cargo sensitive feedback between SNX17 and MTM1.

papers.title: Application of organic fertilisation such as poultry manure enhanced carbohydrate, fat and vitamin C contents of Huckleberry (Solanum scabrum) more than mineral fertilisation in Buea-Cameroon
authors: G. N. A. T. Nkeudem Asoba
papers.abstract: Huckleberry (Solanum scabrum), is a vital indigenous leafy vegetable in sub-Saharan Africa(SSA) and Cameroon, serving as a rich source of vitamins, proteins, and minerals. This study evaluated the nutritional composition, growth, and yield parameters of huckleberry produced using organic and inorganic fertilizers in Buea. A randomized complete block experiment with four blocks compared four fertilisation regimes: pig manure, poultry manure, control, and urea. 6 weeks after planting (WAP), growth parameters; plant height, leaf number and leaf area were measured alongside cumulative yield. Harvested samples were analysed to determine total protein, carbohydrate, fat, and vitamin C contents. Data were subjected to analyse using a two-way analysis of variance. Fertilizer application significantly (P<0.05) enhanced plant performance compared to the unfertilized control. At 8 WAP, urea had the most vigorous vegetative growth, having the highest mean plant height (25.92 cm), maximum leaf count (29.38), and total yield (20.72 tons/ha). Nutritionally, urea produced the highest total protein content (290.30 mg/100 g), but reduced vitamin C level (24.20 mg/100 g) below the baseline of the control (27.53 mg/100 g). Poultry manure had the highest content of carbohydrates (6.52%), fats (7.8%), and vitamin C (42.57 mg/100 g). The study demonstrates a clear trade-off between crop yield and specific nutritional attributes based on nutrient sources. While urea enhanced plant growth and yield, organic amendments like poultry manure improved the micronutrients like carbohydrate and fat composition of huckleberries. Future work should focus on integrated application of poultry and pig manure with urea to see their effects of huckleberry performance, nutrient contents and soil health. Keywords: fertilizer, huckleberry, urea, poultry manure and pig manure

papers.title: Large-scale forward genetics reveals genetically separable components of plant cell proliferative capacity
papers.abstract: Plant cell cultures underpin regeneration, transformation and emerging applications in biotechnology and plant cell agriculture, yet the genetic determinants of proliferative performance remain poorly characterized. Here, we combined large-scale forward genetics with automated image-based phenotyping to quantify 27,648 calli representing 2,880 Arabidopsis thaliana T-DNA insertion lines. Of these, 2,456 lines produced calli smaller than the WT population mean, whereas only 190 produced larger calli, revealing a strongly asymmetric phenotypic distribution. Enhanced callus growth was not consistently associated with increased vegetative growth, indicating that these traits can be genetically uncoupled. Validation of selected high-growth mutants in suspension culture identified lines with enhanced biomass accumulation, while serial propagation revealed independent variation in sustained proliferative capacity. Thus, callus growth, whole-plant growth, short-term suspension biomass accumulation and sustained proliferation represent distinct, not necessarily coupled components of proliferative performance. These findings establish a scalable framework for identifying genetic determinants relevant to the development of improved plant cell production lines.
